items.title: [@waline/client] @waline/client vulnerable to stored XSS through unsanitized comment edit previews
items.summary:
Summary@waline/client renders the comment editor's live preview with marked and no sanitizer (utils/markdown.ts), and the preview is injected with v-html.When a comment is edited, the editor is seeded with the comment's raw, un-sanitized body (orig).Only administrators and the comment owner can edit. So an administrator who clicks Edit on an attacker's comment renders that attacker's raw HTML in their own session: an unauthenticated commenter achieves privilege-escalation stored XSS against a moderator with a single Edit click.Detailspackages/client/src/utils/markdown.ts:18-37 renders markdown with marked and returns the raw HTML with no sanitization (the client bundles no DOMPurify):return marked.parse(parseEmoji(content, emojiMap)) as string;packages/client/src/components/CommentBox.vue:onMounted(() => { if (props.edit?.objectId) editor.value = props.edit.orig; // :509 raw comment body watchImmediate(() => editor.value, (value) => { previewText.value = parseMarkdown(value, { ... }); // :519 runs immediately on mount });});
watchImmediate runs the callback synchronously at mount, so previewText is populated with the unsanitized render as soon as the box mounts in edit mode.v-show (not v-if) means the v-html node is present in the DOM (display:none), so an fires without the moderator ever opening the preview tab.The tainted value is the attacker's raw comment. packages/server/src/controller/comment.js:41 sets comment.orig = comment.comment for any logged-in user before :55 runs DOMPurify, so orig is the pre-sanitization body. formatCmt returns it to logged-in users, and CommentCard.vue:104 shows the Edit button to admin or owner.Proof of conceptAs an anonymous user, post a comment whose body is the payload below via POST /api/comment:POST /api/comment{ "url": "/any-post", "nick": "a", "comment": "" }On the public page the server sanitizes the display copy (markdown-it -> DOMPurify), so nothing fires for ordinary readers and the comment shows as a broken image. The raw body is stored in orig.As an administrator or the comment owner, click Edit on that comment during normal moderation.CommentBox mounts, seeds the editor with the raw orig, and watchImmediate immediately renders it through parseMarkdown (marked, no sanitizer) into the v-html preview node. Because the preview uses v-show (display:none), that node is already in the DOM without opening the preview tab, so onerror fires at once in the admin's session and exfiltrates their localStorage JWT.The server's own comment guard strips this same on the stored display copy, which is why the public listing is safe; the edit preview is the unguarded path.ImpactThe waline JWT is in same-origin localStorage, so the payload can read it, yielding full administrative account takeover.Suggested fixSanitize parseMarkdown's output with DOMPurify before returning it, mirroring the server guard: add dompurify to @waline/client and wrap the return in DOMPurify.sanitize(..., { FORBID_TAGS: ['form','input','style'], FORBID_ATTR: ['autoplay','style'] }).Referenceshttps://github.com/walinejs/waline/security/advisories/GHSA-crj3-q72p-ggqmhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-64670https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-crj3-q72p-ggqm
